Your chainsaws have at least 5 properties such as length of the "guide bar" (Schwertlaenge), chain width, electric or motor chainsaw.
After your customer told you the properties, you can start ordering the parts from various online sources (in parallel).
After the parts arrive you have to do a manual inspection of all parts, and then assemble the parts.
During production, you regularly send updates to your customer.
After producing the first saw you send it to your customer.
If he likes it, the rest of his order are produced.

trace.reason: Check documented guidance related to staged production, customer feedback, and conditional continuation.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

result.rule: When the description states that work proceeds concurrently and that a later step must wait until all of that work is complete: Model the concurrent work as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel gateway before the dependent step.

When the description explicitly states that an activity follows the process start or another activity: connect the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows in the stated order, preserving any intervening gateways and branches

When the description states that approval is followed by required activities and that the process closes after those activities: Connect the approval outcome through all required follow-up activities to the process end, preserving any ordering or parallelism stated in the description.

When the description says that work can branch into parallel or conditional activities, or that a setback returns the process to earlier work: Connect the affected activities with sequence flows, using gateways to represent the described branching or synchronization and preserving any stated return flow.
